subject: Cap / Floor Tier Reconciliation — orderform redline logistics
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Claire Emerson <claire.emerson@glenmonthealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 Dec 2028 08:23:00 -0800
Subject: Cap / Floor tier reconciliation — redline and logistics

Hi Claire — attaching our redline of the Order Form and a short worksheet that shows how the cap/floor cascade would compute across the three SKU buckets Glenmont asked about. Key asks on our side: please confirm whether Glenmont expects the caps to be evaluated "per-sku" or "portfolio-level" at each billing period, and whether the floor triggers should be measured on committed spend or invoiced usage.

Highlights in the attached PDF:
- Section 2.1 (Order Schedule): proposed language that makes caps cascade top-down across tiers (we added an example row).
- Section 3.4 (Minimums / Floors): two options (A: per-sku floor, B: blended floor across the three SKUs).

A couple quick notes so legal/procurement aligns properly:
- If Glenmont needs per-sku floor enforcement, our billing system will require SKU-level meters and this may change implementation timing by ~2 weeks.
- If you accept the blended floor approach we circled, the operational lift is smaller and the true-up is performed quarterly (rather than monthly).

Can you confirm which interpretation Glenmont prefers? If you prefer, we can produce a short worked example pulled into the OrderForm_v3.xlsx to show month-by-month implications.

Attachments: Glenmont_Redline_20281203.pdf (redline with comments), OrderForm_v3.xlsx (worked example)

Thanks —
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
pri ya.natarajan@redwood.com
Press 2 for discounts (just kidding)

From: Claire Emerson <claire.emerson@glenmonthealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Glenmont Health Procurement <procurement@glenmonthealth.com>
Date: Sun, 3 Dec 2028 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cap / Floor tier reconciliation — redline and logistics

Priya — thanks for sending this over and for the clear worksheet. Procurement and finance discussed internally and a few clarifications from our side:

- Our preference is option B (blended floor across the three SKUs) to avoid SKU-level billing complexity.
- However, procurement needs explicit language that the blended floor calculation will be performed on "invoiced usage" and that a quarterly true-up will be the official reconciliation cadence.
- We also need an explicit cap cascade example in the contract because our auditors require an illustrative calculation with the same sample data that appears in OrderForm_v3.xlsx.

I'm attaching procurement's suggested insertion for Section 3.4 (small paragraph) — happy to take Redwood's counterlanguage. If we can agree on the wording, procurement can route the final Order Form for signature.

Claire Emerson
Senior Sourcing Manager, Glenmont Health
procurement@glenmonthealth.com

Attachment: GLN_Procurement_Insert_20281203.docx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Dec 2028 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cap / Floor tier reconciliation — redline and logistics

On Sun, Dec 3, 2028 at 08:23 AM Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Claire — attaching our redline of the Order Form and a short worksheet that shows how the cap/floor cascade would compute across the three SKU buckets Glenmont asked about.
> 
> Highlights in the attached PDF:
> - Section 2.1 (Order Schedule): proposed language that makes caps cascade top-down across tiers (we added an example row).

Folks — quick legal/commercial notes inline:

1) Blended floor (Option B) is acceptable from a risk standpoint but we need to add a sentence that the blended floor is computed after applying any per-SKU discounts and usage credits. That avoids a situation where discounts are applied after the floor calculation (which materially changes economics).

2) Wording suggestion for 3.4 (to propose back to Claire):
"For the avoidance of doubt, the Minimum Payment (the 'Floor') shall be calculated on the aggregate invoiced usage across the SKU set listed in the Order Schedule after application of all discounts, credits, and rebates. Reconciliation shall occur on a quarterly basis, with any shortfall invoiced to Customer within thirty (30) days of the reconciliation period close."

3) Cap cascade example: we should include both a per-month snapshot and a quarterly aggregation example in the OrderForm spreadsheet. The per-month snapshot is what operations will use for realtime throttling/alerts; the quarterly aggregation is what finance will use for true-up.

4) We should confirm whether Glenmont expects the cap to be hard enforcement (service refusal) at the threshold or merely an overage price applied. If it's service refusal, that has to flow into the SLA and product feature gating.

Marissa — can you review the suggested clause and the attached Concession_Matrix_v2.xlsx and confirm if commercial is willing to accept the blended floor with the "after discounts" sentence? If yes, I'll add the language to the redline and prepare the final Order Form for sourcing signature.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Manager, Commercial Contracts
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Claire Emerson <claire.emerson@glenmonthealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Dec 2028 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cap / Floor tier reconciliation — orderform redline logistics

Claire — thanks for the fast turnaround and for the procurement insert. Per Karthik's suggestion, we've added a short clarifying sentence to 3.4 that the blended floor is computed on "aggregate invoiced usage after application of discounts, credits and rebates". I've attached an updated Concession_Matrix_v2.xlsx that shows the math both per-month and aggregated quarterly.

Proposed next steps:
- Please confirm Glenmont is comfortable with the "after discounts" phrasing and the quarterly true-up cadence.
- If yes, Glenmont procurement can accept the redline and we'll issue a final Order Form for signature.
- Marissa — if commercial signs off on the concession matrix by EOD Thursday, I'll proceed to prepare DocuSign.

Attachments: Concession_Matrix_v2.xlsx (worked examples), OrderForm_v3.xlsx (updated with quarterly example)

Thanks —
